title: Harden Skill verification cancellation and schema binding
goal: Ensure standalone Skill verification observes cancellation, built-in normalization only executes against its declared schema, and outputs rejected by their executor never count as verified.
context: Audit found two contract-boundary gaps: standalone verification lacked cancellation checks around awaited work, and the built-in text.normalize executor did not bind execution or verification to its own schema identifiers. Regression coverage also needs to prove executeVerified rejects a false verifier result. The first M3 run exposed an existing integration fixture that declared text.normalize as its executor while using unrelated schema IDs; the fixture must declare the built-in schema IDs to represent a valid contract.
forbidden_changes: Do not bypass policy, executor resolution, Agent scope, or verification.
Do not enable new capabilities or alter workspace behavior.
Do not change unrelated provider, UI, or app project files.
Do not change the declared text.normalize schema identifiers or silently adapt mismatched Skill manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Standalone verification checks cancellation before and after awaited operations.
A cancelled verification task throws CancellationError rather than returning a verification result.
text.normalize rejects execution and verification when manifest schema identifiers differ from its declared contract.
executeVerified throws verificationFailed when the resolved executor rejects its own output.
Regression tests cover cancellation, schema mismatch, and failed output verification.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass.
Verified execution continues to respect an explicitly denied policy.
Regression fixtures use valid JSON so each test exercises the intended schema or verification path.
Imported Skills that declare the built-in normalizer use the normalizer's exact schema identifiers.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: If any cancellation, schema-binding, or verification regression fails, inspect the exact boundary, make the smallest in-scope correction, and rerun all required gates before merge.
